title: Representational Homomorphism Predicts and Improves Compositional Generalization In Transformer Language Model
authors: Zhiyu An; Wan Du
task_custom_name: Adapted SCAN (noise injection, primitive coverage manipulations)
arch_detail: Small decoder-only Transformers trained from scratch; depth ablated 1-10 layers; layer-wise MSE-based Homomorphism Error metric using linear, bilinear, and MLP operators; no pretraining (to avoid data spoilage)

repr_analysis_finding: HE predicts OOD compositional generalization under noise injection (R2=0.73); model depth has minimal effect on HE or OOD accuracy; noise tokens increase modifier HE while sequence HE stays stable; HE-regularization reduces HE and improves OOD accuracy
relevance_sigma_justification: Core sigma-trap study: introduces Homomorphism Error, a representation-level metric of compositional structure failure, shows it predicts OOD compositional generalization (R2=0.73), and demonstrates that regularizing HE during training significantly improves OOD accuracy (p=0.023) on an adapted SCAN benchmark.
relevance_alignment_justification: Not an alignment paper, but diagnosing and controlling internal compositional structure of models (via a regularizable representational metric) is a step toward interpretability and steering relevant to understanding goal misgeneralization; no explicit safety discussion.
limitations_text: Experiments on synthetic data with precisely controlled compositional structure; real-world language adds semantic ambiguity, context dependence, and irregular constructions. Evaluation on relatively small Transformer models; behavior of homomorphism error in large-scale pretrained LMs remains open.
open_questions_text: Apply homomorphism error analysis to established compositional benchmarks using natural language; investigate how homomorphism error scales with model size and pretraining data; explore compositionally-aware architecture search and training procedures.
other_metrics_reported: Homomorphism Error (modifier and sequence HE, layer-wise MSE averaged over linear/bilinear/MLP operators); R2 of HE-OOD accuracy regression
notes: Main-form ood values = baseline decoder-only Transformer on adapted SCAN, 0 noise tokens (~47%). No ID accuracies reported; study reports OOD accuracy only, with mean and std across 5 seeds. Under review (preprint); code/data open-sourced.

title: Hierarchical Poset Decoding for Compositional Generalization in Language
authors: Yinuo Guo; Zeqi Lin; Jian-Guang Lou; Dongmei Zhang
arch_detail: Hierarchical Poset Decoding (HPD): encoder-decoder with poset-based sketch prediction, phrase-table primitive prediction, and traversal path prediction; baselines: LSTM+Attention, Transformer, Universal Transformer (Keysers et al. 2020), Seq2Tree, CGPS; ablations replace sketch predictor or remove hierarchical mechanism
train_data_note: CFQ over Freebase, MCD1/MCD2/MCD3 splits; accuracy = % of examples correctly parsed to gold SPARQL meaning representations; SPARQL simplified via merging similar triples in one baseline block
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; mean MCD accuracy 69.0% stated directly for HPD, 56.7% for Seq2Tree-based sketch ablation
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy; poset structure is an output-decoding constraint, not a measured representation property
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly attacks compositional generalization failure on CFQ MCD splits; hierarchical poset decoding enforces partial permutation invariance, improving mean MCD accuracy to 69.0% vs sub-20% seq2seq baselines, with ablations isolating the permutation-invariance and hierarchical mechanisms.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely an architectural decoding method for compositional generalization in semantic parsing.
limitations_text: Break-down analysis: sketch prediction fails on 8.7%/24.9%/25.2% of MCD1/2/3 test cases because the sequence encoder does not capture implicit syntactic structure; primitive prediction has low precision (34.4-35.0%) from a simple phrase table; traversal path prediction fails on 11.7%/15.5%/7.0% of cases due to many candidate paths.
open_questions_text: Future work: enhance the encoder with compositionality and build attention between encoder and hierarchical poset decoder; improve primitive prediction recall via contextual information; reduce the number of candidate primitives for traversal path prediction.
other_metrics_reported: Component-level metrics per split: Sketch Prediction accuracy (91.3/75.1/74.8); Primitive Prediction precision (34.4/35.0/34.1) and recall (99.9); Traversal Path Prediction precision/recall/F1 (e.g., 96.7/98.9/97.7 on MCD1)
notes: Main-form values = HPD with Seq2Seq-based sketch prediction, mean accuracy 69.0% across MCD splits (stated). Per-split and baseline/ablation values in sub_experiments; means computed from per-split cells where noted. Paper header stamps NeurIPS 2020 despite arXiv ID. Baselines (LSTM+Attention, Transformer, Universal Transformer) from Keysers et al. 2020.

title: Unlocking Compositional Generalization in Pre-trained Models Using Intermediate Representations
authors: Jonathan Herzig; Peter Shaw; Ming-Wei Chang; Kelvin Guu; Panupong Pasupat; Yuan Zhang
arch_detail: T5-small/T5-base seq2seq; two-stage pipeline (Seq2Seq1 predicts intermediate representation, Seq2Seq2 conditions on IR + utterance to generate program); no architectural changes vs baseline
train_data_note: CFQ (MCD splits) and three text-to-SQL datasets (template splits); results averaged over test sets; dev accuracy reported
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; gains quoted as accuracy points (CFQ +14.8, text-to-SQL +15.0 to +19.4)
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy; analyses concern target-program structure (novel structures, program length), not internal representations
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure in pre-trained seq2seq parsers on CFQ MCD and text-to-SQL template splits, showing that structural correspondence of the target representation (intermediate representations, RIR/LIR) unlocks OOD generalization, and analyzing why (novel structures, program length).
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; the work concerns semantic parsing compositional generalization only.
limitations_text: Approach requires customizing new intermediate representations for each formalism; this entails manual work, though it is done only once per formalism (same IRs reused across three text-to-SQL datasets).
other_metrics_reported: Percentage of new structures in dev vs train; average program length in word-pieces
notes: IRs effective only with pre-training (Table 4: no-pretraining +IRs gives +1.8 CFQ, -11.8 text-to-SQL). LIR-ORACLE (gold LIR) boosts CFQ MCD 41.9 to 80.7. Best combo LIRd + RIR. Text-to-SQL not in task vocabulary; task_custom_name left empty, see train_data_note.

title: Compositional Generalization by Learning Analytical Expressions
authors: Qian Liu; Shengnan An; Jian-Guang Lou; Bei Chen; Zeqi Lin; Yan Gao; Bin Zhou; Nanning Zheng; Dongmei Zhang
arch_detail: Memory-augmented model with two cooperative modules (Composer builds parse trees over the input using a Tree-LSTM; Solver generates output expressions), trained end-to-end via hierarchical RL with curriculum learning
train_data_note: SCAN systematicity, distribution-based systematicity, SCAN-ext (productivity), and MiniSCAN (Limit) splits; no extra resources or data augmentation used
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy measured
repr_analysis_finding: Analysis of learned Composer tree structures shows 'twice' behaves differently under different contexts (Fig. 5), indicating context-dependent symbolic structure
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure (the sigma-trap) on SCAN, achieving 100% on systematicity, distribution-based systematicity, productivity (SCAN-ext), and MiniSCAN splits without extra resources; the neurosymbolic design and curriculum are interventions against the gap.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; the work is a compositional generalization method paper with no safety implications discussed.
open_questions_text: Conclusion and Future Work section present but its text is truncated in the excerpt
other_metrics_reported: test accuracy per SCAN task; accuracy vs input length (productivity); train/test accuracy under different learning-rate combinations
notes: Main-form values = LANE on SCAN (100% OOD test accuracy across all tasks); ID accuracies not reported numerically. Ablations (Tab. 3): w/o Composer drops to near-zero (Simple 98.5, Add Jump 0.0, Length 11.1, Around Right 0.0, MCD1 5.3, MCD2 0.7, MCD3 2.6); w/o curriculum learning never converges (all 0); w/o simplicity-based reward fails on Around Right.

title: Compositional Generalization in Multilingual Semantic Parsing over Wikidata
authors: Ruixiang Cui; Rahul Aralikatte; Heather Lent; Daniel Hershcovich
task_custom_name: MCWQ (Multilingual Compositional Wikidata Questions) - multilingual semantic parsing over Wikidata, MCD splits
arch_detail: T5/mT5 seq2seq models with RIR (repeat-and-insert) decoder; mT5-small+RIR and mT5-base+RIR; pretrained multilingual encoders; monolingual English training + zero-shot cross-lingual transfer to Hebrew, Kannada, Chinese
train_data_note: MCWQ: multilingual parallel questions over Wikidata derived from CFQ via machine translation (MT) with gold-translation test-intersection-gold; models trained on English, zero-shot evaluated on Hebrew/Kannada/Chinese; 155-item intersection test sets
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; comparisons are descriptive (monolingual vs zero-shot accuracy)
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence metric measured
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly evaluates compositional generalization (MCD splits, compound divergence) in multilingual semantic parsing and demonstrates catastrophic failure of cross-lingual compositional generalization (<0.3% zero-shot vs 38.3% monolingual), a clear instance of compositional generalization breakdown.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; the paper is a dataset contribution and behavioral evaluation for multilingual semantic parsing.
open_questions_text: Whether cross-lingual compositional transfer will be more effective on related languages (e.g., English to German) remains to be investigated; potential cause of failure is that the four languages belong to different language families with low linguistic similarity.
other_metrics_reported: BLEU score of predicted SPARQL queries; error categorization (missing/extra/wrong property, missing/extra/wrong entity, multiple errors)
notes: Main-form ood values = monolingual mT5-small+RIR on English MCDmean (38.3%). Zero-shot cross-lingual mT5-small+RIR is below 0.3% accuracy. ID (random split) English exact match not numerically given in excerpt. Results averaged over models trained on three MCD splits, not seeds.

title: Data Factors for Better Compositional Generalization
authors: Xiang Zhou; Yichen Jiang; Mohit Bansal

relevance_sigma_justification: Directly investigates the sigma-trap: Transformer models trained from scratch fail on SCAN/COGS compositional splits, and the paper identifies data-complexity factors (diversity, example repetition frequency, example difficulty) that modulate compositional generalization failure, bridging diagnostic-dataset failures and pretrained-model successes; no link to training dynamics or flatness.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; the paper is an empirical analysis of data factors for compositional generalization with no safety discussion.
other_metrics_reported: Example-difficulty metric: earliest training step at which an example is predicted correctly for 10 consecutive checkpoints; prototype-based difficulty metrics for sub-sampling

title: Iterative Decoding for Compositional Generalization in Transformers
authors: Luana Ruiz; Joshua Ainslie; Santiago Ontañón
task_custom_name: Cartesian product dataset (Ontanón et al. 2021)
arch_detail: Transformer seq2seq with relative attention (radius r=8) and copy decoding variants; iterative decoding decomposes mapping into intermediate steps fed back as inputs until end-of-iteration token, with short/long intermediate input and row/token decoding scenarios
train_data_note: PCFG (Hupkes et al. 2020) random/productivity/systematicity splits; Cartesian product easy (ID) + hard productivity splits; CFQ MCD1
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure (a core sigma-trap phenomenon) in transformers on PCFG productivity/systematicity, Cartesian product, and CFQ MCD1 splits, showing seq2seq transformers fail to learn unrolled iterations while iterative decoding largely closes the gap; no connection to training dynamics or schema coherence.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; purely a decoding-method study for compositional generalization in sequence learning.
limitations_text: Iterative decoding underperforms seq2seq on CFQ MCD1 (32.5% vs 37.1%); it only generalizes to longer iterations that were unrolled during training (row-decoding fails when extra token pairs are added); PCFG iterative decoding test accuracy still below training accuracy.
notes: Main-form accuracy left empty: results are per-dataset/per-split (Tables 1-3), no single headline number. PCFG Table 1 values not numerically reproduced in excerpt (prose: iterative decoding with relative attention exceeds 90% test accuracy on productivity and systematicity splits), so no PCFG sub_experiments. Cartesian product sentence accuracies (Table 2, relative attention r=8) and CFQ MCD1 (Table 3) in sub_experiments; 'easy' test split treated as ID.

title: Structural generalization in COGS: Supertagging is (almost) all you need
authors: Alban Petit; Caio Corro; François Yvon
arch_detail: Neural graph-based semantic parser extended with supertagging step (ILP valency constraints, companionship principle), argument identification as maximum matching, factor-graph weakly-supervised loss, incremental early stopping
train_data_note: COGS dataset; training on in-distribution data with incremental early stopping (freezes part of the network) to prevent overfitting
effect_size_notes: Paper reports a 23.9 point increase from 51.1 to 75.0 accuracy on Obj-to-subj PP attributable to the incremental early-stopping training procedure
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy measured; supertagging accuracy is a pipeline-internal metric, not a representation analysis
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly addresses compositional (structural) generalization failure on COGS by adding supertagging with ILP valency constraints, matching-based argument identification, and incremental early stopping, reaching high accuracy on structural generalization cases where baselines score near zero - a targeted fix for the sigma-trap.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; a semantic parsing method paper with no safety discussion.
limitations_text: Cannot predict supertags unseen during training (meta-grammars could overcome this); ILP solver may be slow in more realistic settings; pipeline's local predictions cannot use argument identification scores to fix earlier errors
other_metrics_reported: Overall accuracy (mostly lexical generalization, 85.7% of test set); per-case structural generalization accuracies (Obj to subj PP, PP recursion, CP recursion); word-level supertagging accuracy with/without ILP
notes: COGS test contains 1,000 sentences per generalization case. Best config reaches 75.0 on Obj-to-subj PP (vs 51.1 without early stopping); PP recursion and CP recursion predicted perfectly; supertagging accuracy with ILP 90.2 vs 71.6 without for Obj-to-subj PP. Overall COGS accuracy not extractable from excerpt.

title: When Can Transformers Ground and Compose: Insights from Compositional Generalization Benchmarks
authors: Ankur Sikarwar; Arkil Patel; Navin Goyal
task_custom_name: ReaSCAN (grounded navigation); gSCAN (GSRR splits); RefEx (novel grounded referring-expression task)
arch_detail: GroCoT: attention-only transformer, command + world-state embeddings concatenated, stacked multi-head attention blocks with residual connections, 36-way softmax over grid cells; a single self-attention layer with a single head generalizes on RefEx; learned positional embeddings only for three-attr-rel variant; LLM baselines: GPT-3, Codex (few-shot in-context)
train_data_note: RefEx: 90K train / 2.5K val / 2.5K test per variant; C2-deeper: 100K sampled train + 6,000 C2 test examples, 4,500 depth-3 test examples; ReaSCAN and gSCAN used for main experiments
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-coherence proxy measured (no CKA/RSA/compositionality score)
repr_analysis_finding: Linear probe of target location in encoder representations: near-perfect localization accuracy on A1/A2/B1/B2 (up to ~100) but near 0 on A3 and C1 and 23.4 on C2, identifying target identification as the main OOD challenge; layer 0 (input embeddings) and random-embedding baselines also probed
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly probes grounded compositional generalization (the sigma-trap): shows a simple attention-only transformer generalizes on ReaSCAN, gSCAN and RefEx novel attribute compositions, isolates target identification as the core OOD challenge, and shows the ReaSCAN C2 depth-generalization split is unfair, with transformers generalizing on an amended deeper split.
relevance_alignment_justification: No alignment or safety discussion; indirect relevance via mechanistic insight into when transformers compose (single attention head suffices) and LLM failure on grounded compositionality.
notes: Main-benchmark accuracies (ReaSCAN/gSCAN/RefEx default settings) are not present in the excerpt; sub_experiments carry Table 13 action-seq accuracies (with ground-truth target locations; caption labels gSCAN but split names A1-A3/B1-B2/C1 match ReaSCAN) and LLM nonsense-grounded RefEx results. Metric = action sequence accuracy / target localization accuracy.

title: Compositional Generalization for Natural Language Interfaces to Web APIs
authors: Saghar Hosseini; Ahmed Hassan Awadallah; Yu Su
task_custom_name: Okapi NL2API (natural language to executable web API calls)
ood_difficulty_metric_name: compound divergence (DBCA) applied to the Length split; Length vs Program split difficulty comparison

train_data_note: Okapi: 22,508 English questions, 9,019 unique API calls, three domains (Document, Email, Calendar); non-synthetic, low-resource; Length and Program splits; SCAN used for comparison

relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; the work is a dataset and baseline evaluation for compositional semantic parsing of web API calls.
other_metrics_reported: error-type analysis of erroneous predictions (wrong/missing/extra parameters, invalid calls, annotation mistakes) for T5-Base

title: Revisiting the Compositional Generalization Abilities of Neural Sequence Models
authors: Arkil Patel; Satwik Bhattamishra; Phil Blunsom; Navin Goyal
arch_detail: Standard seq2seq models: LSTM and Transformer; LSTM capacity swept 6.7K-354K params; SCAN/Colors embedding analyses on LSTM (t-SNE, distance metrics)

title: Measuring Compositional Generalization: A Comprehensive Method on Realistic Data
authors: Daniel Keysers; Nathanael Schärli; Nathan Scales; Hylke Buisman; Daniel Furrer; Sergii Kashubin; Nikola Momchev; Danila Sinopalnikov; Lukasz Stafiniak; Tibor Tihon; Dmitry Tsarkov; Xiao Wang; Marc van Zee; Olivier Bousquet

title: Recursive Decoding: A Situated Cognition Approach to Compositional Generation in Grounded Language Understanding
authors: Matthew Setzler; Scott Howland; Lauren Phillips
arch_detail: Recursive Decoding (RD): training/decoding procedure for seq2seq models predicting one token at a time, incrementally updating and re-encoding the gSCAN grid-world input at each decoder step; baseline = standard attention-based seq2seq from gSCAN (Ruis et al.); also randomized initial-orientation variant
train_data_note: gSCAN grid-world; original and randomized initial-orientation datasets plus intermediate-world control dataset; control trained 200,000 batches; RD models <72 GPU-hours, baseline <24 GPU-hours, single 16GB P100, ~1200 GPU-hours total
train_regime_other: Recursive Decoding: model predicts one output token at a time; intermediate world states re-encoded as fresh inputs each decoder step
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; comparisons reported as exact-match percentages with std (e.g., RD 84.42±3.24 on Length vs baseline/SotA 2.10±0.05)
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy measured; analyses focus on agent ending-position heatmaps and non-canonical solution behavior

relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets decode-side compositional generalization failure in gSCAN, achieving dramatic gains on novel-direction (0.0% to 43.6%) and length-extrapolation (2.1% to 84.4%) tasks, with failure analysis of the baseline and an experimental control isolating the procedural innovation.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; framed purely as compositional generalization in grounded language understanding.
limitations_extractor: Excerpt discusses baseline failure modes but no explicit limitations section for RD; partial excerpt may omit discussion section
open_questions_extractor: Paper signals implications for naturalistic grounded language understanding and seq2seq generally, but no explicit open questions in excerpt
other_metrics_reported: Exact match per gSCAN task; non-canonical solution rate (86.32±9.00% valid, 37.45% non-canonical); ending-position heatmap analysis; null-model analysis of error-correcting solutions
notes: Main-form values = RD on Length task (OOD) and gSCAN Random split as ID (0.9922±0.0016). RD Random = RD trained on randomized initial-orientation dataset. n_seeds_value 3 inferred from 'Three instances of the Baseline model' and '2/3 models' statements (control/random-orientation runs); per-table run counts not explicit. gSCAN tasks treated as separate splits in sub_experiments.

title: Compositional Generalization without Trees using Multiset Tagging and Latent Permutations
authors: Matthias Lindemann; Alexander Koller; Ivan Titov
arch_detail: Two-stage: multiset tagger predicts a multiset of output tokens per input token, then a permutation model arranges tokens via an entropy-regularized linear program (backprop through solver); RoBERTa encoder; variant w/o pretraining uses biLSTM + GloVe
train_data_note: COGS (structural splits OS/CP/PP), ATIS (iid + length split: few conjuncts train to longer logical forms), Okapi (length splits in Calendar/Doc/Email domains)
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; comparisons via accuracy mean and SD over 5 runs
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence or compositionality proxy; analysis is stage-wise output accuracy (multiset vs permutation), not internal representations
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly attacks compositional generalization failure in semantic parsing: structural generalization on COGS (first tree-free model with high accuracy on deeper recursion depth) and length generalization on ATIS/Okapi, attributing errors to multiset vs permutation stages; mechanism-level treatment without tree inductive biases.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; the work is about semantic parsing compositional generalization only.
other_metrics_reported: Stage-wise breakdown: multiset accuracy (Freq), permutation accuracy (Seq, Seq/Freq); training runtime 2h vs 12h for L'23; outlier run noted on ATIS length (18% accuracy)
notes: Main form: ATIS iid (ID) and length split (OOD) with RoBERTa-based model, 5 runs. Screening hint of 10 seeds contradicted by excerpt (5 runs); n_seeds_value corrected to 5. ATIS/Okapi not in task vocabulary; tasks_secondary=other.

authors: Xinyun Chen; Chen Liang; Adams Wei Yu; Dawn Song; Denny Zhou

train_data_note: SCAN trained without additional data; compositional MT uses 11,000 English-French pairs (1,000 introduce pseudoword 'daxy'); CFG parsing uses a curriculum of 100-150 samples enumerating grammar constructors

effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy measured
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly addresses compositional generalization failure (the sigma-trap) via a neural-symbolic stack machine achieving 100% across four domains (SCAN, few-shot instructions, compositional MT, CFG parsing), including length generalization to inputs 500x longer than training samples.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; the paper is a compositional generalization method paper with no safety implications discussed.

title: Compositional Generalization for Primitive Substitutions
authors: Yuanpeng Li; Liang Zhao; Jianyu Wang; Joel Hestness
task_custom_name: SCAN Primitive substitution (Jump, TurnLeft, SCAN-ADJ); few-shot learning (Lake et al. 2019); EN-FR compositional MT

title: Uncontrolled Lexical Exposure Leads to Overestimation of Compositional Generalization in Pretrained Models
authors: Najoung Kim; Tal Linzen; Paul Smolensky
arch_detail: T5-base and T5-small (pretrained) finetuned on modified COGS training sets; context-controlled lexical items replaced by novel character sequences or special tokens with novel embeddings
train_data_note: Finetuned on modified COGS training sets (context-controlled lexical items substituted); 300K steps ~398 epochs, no early stopping; exposure examples learned to 100%; batch 32, AdamW, linear scheduling
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly quantifies compositional generalization failure in pretrained T5: under controlled lexical exposure (novel character sequences and novel-embedding tokens) COGS generalization drops from 83% to 6-32%, exposing pretraining-data leakage as the cause of overestimated compositional generalization and demonstrating inverse scaling with pretraining corpus size; central to the sigma-trap diagnosis.
relevance_alignment_justification: Concerns overestimation of generalization performance in pretrained models due to evaluation leakage, bearing on trustworthy capability assessment of foundation models, but it does not discuss alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization directly.
other_metrics_reported: Auxiliary test sets Test-Lex and Gen (Lex only); exposure-example accuracy; development set accuracy
notes: Main = T5-base with randomly initialized novel embeddings (Expt 2). Unmodified COGS baseline Gen = 83.3%, Test-ID ~99.8%; character-sequence setup Gen = 64-69% (range only, Table 1 not included); paper frames ~51pp overestimation; inverse scaling with pretraining corpus size in T5-small.

title: A Neuroscience-Inspired Dual-Process Model of Compositional Generalization
authors: Alex Noviello; Claas Beger; Jacob Groner; Kevin Ellis; Weinan Sun
arch_detail: MIRAGE dual-process model: System 1 = meta-trained Transformer Neural Decomposer (single-step compositional decomposition); System 2 = Schema Engine (rule-based, prioritized schemas, episodic bindings); iterative refinement loop; baselines: vanilla Transformer and Transformer+SC_Library prompt
train_data_note: System 1 meta-trained to perform single-step decomposition on a stream of random grammars; evaluated task-agnostically (zero-shot) on all SCAN splits
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy measured; the schema library is symbolic and interpretability is discussed qualitatively via stepwise traces
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly confronts the sigma-trap: systematic compositional generalization failure in deep learning. MIRAGE achieves >99% accuracy on all SCAN splits (including Length, Add prim, Template designed to foil seq2seq models) via a dual-process neuro-inspired architecture, with ablations isolating schema priorities, iterative refinement, and accurate schemas as causes of systematic behavior; offers a processing and interpretability account of why compositional failure occurs and how it can be overcome.
relevance_alignment_justification: Not an alignment/safety paper, but its externalized, stepwise-verifiable schema traces and cognitive-architecture framing speak to interpretability and transparency concerns that are adjacent to AI safety; no direct treatment of goal misgeneralization.
limitations_text: MIRAGE relies on reliable extraction of a consistent grammar; robustness to noisy or incomplete schemas is not yet addressed; evaluation is limited to SCAN.
open_questions_text: Extend the schema extractor with probabilistic rule learning and active retrieval for noisy schemas; apply the architecture to more complex reasoning tasks; use its inspectable states to test neuroscientific hypotheses about HPC-PFC interactions during planning.
notes: Main-form values = MIRAGE on SCAN (Simple treated as ID, Length as representative OOD). Table 1 reports mean +/- SEM over 4 runs. Ablations (prose): removing schema priorities drops accuracy from 99.6% to 71.9%; corrupted schemas collapse to ~0%; single-pass end-to-end mapping fails to generalize.

title: Compositional generalization in a deep seq2seq model by separating syntax and semantics
authors: Jake Russin; Jason Jo; Randall C. O'Reilly; Yoshua Bengio
arch_detail: Syntactic Attention: seq2seq NMT (Bahdanau attention setup) with separate syntactic and semantic attention heads, inspired by distinct neural systems for syntax and semantics; no hand-engineered features or extra supervision
train_data_note: SCAN; add-jump split (jump held out except basic context, up to 32 added jump commands in scaling experiment); template splits: jump around right, primitive right, primitive opposite right, primitive around right
effect_size_notes: No effect size reported; mean accuracies with SDs across random samples
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy measured; attention visualizations are qualitative, not a scalar coherence metric
repr_analysis_finding: Attention visualizations (Figures 10-15) show the model applies the same syntactic rules learned on other verbs to the novel verb 'jump' on test examples; failure mode occurs when the model fails to attend to the correct sequence of commands
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly studies compositional generalization failure on SCAN add-jump and template splits, showing RNN seq2seq models fail catastrophically (12.5%) while the syntax/semantics-separated Syntactic Attention nearly solves it, with attention analyses of the underlying mechanism - squarely a sigma-trap investigation.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; a cognitive-science-inspired seq2seq architecture paper with no safety discussion.
limitations_text: Syntactic Attention fails on Primitive opposite right (10.5%) and Primitive around right (28.9%) template splits where the left-right symmetry is violated; attention mechanism sometimes fails to attend to the correct command sequence
open_questions_text: Further research required on whether a model implementing similar principles can perform well on template splits where the symmetry between left and right is violated
other_metrics_reported: Mean accuracy (%) with SD over 5 random samples; attention weight visualizations
notes: Main form = Syntactic Attention on add-jump split with 2 jump examples (text cites 99.997%, Table 4 shows 100.0 +/- 0.01). Intro baselines on standard add-jump: best RNN (GRU+attn) 12.5%, CNN 69.2%. Screening hint of 25 runs contradicted by explicit 5 random samples in excerpt.

title: Compositional Generalization and Decomposition in Neural Program Synthesis
authors: Kensen Shi; Joey Hong; Manzil Zaheer; Pengcheng Yin; Charles Sutton
task_custom_name: RobustFill (string transformation program synthesis)
arch_detail: Transformer program synthesizers with novel decomposition-inspired attention mechanisms vs natural Transformer baselines; trained on SCAN and RobustFill; zero-shot (SCAN 10k steps, RobustFill 1M steps, batch 128) and few-shot (20 train + 20 test examples, 30 epochs) settings
train_data_note: SCAN and RobustFill benchmarks; benchmark suite characterizes axes of compositional generalization (length generalization, novel subroutine combinations, others)
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes; results only in figures/tables referenced but not reproduced in excerpt
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy measured
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly addresses compositional generalization failure (the sigma-trap) in neural program synthesis: characterizes axes of compositional/OOD generalization (length generalization, novel subroutine combination), introduces a SCAN/RobustFill-based benchmark suite, and proposes decomposition-inspired attention mechanisms, finding modified Transformers beat baselines but tasks remain challenging.
relevance_alignment_justification: No alignment or safety discussion; indirect relevance via compositional robustness of neural code generators, an adjacent domain to goal misgeneralization.
notes: No numeric results present in the excerpt (Tables 1-2 and Figures 4-7 referenced but values not reproduced); mean test accuracy over 3 random initializations with 1-SD error bars reported in figures; modified Transformer models generally outperform baselines but tasks remain challenging.

title: Learning to Recombine and Resample Data for Compositional Generalization
authors: Ekin Akyürek; Afra Feyza Akyürek; Jacob Andreas
task_custom_name: SIGMORPHON 2018 morphology (Spanish, Swahili, Turkish)
arch_detail: R&R learned data augmentation: prototype-based generative model recombines training examples and resamples generated examples to encourage extrapolation; applied to ordinary neural seq2seq models (Bahdanau et al. 2015 style); VAE variant in Table 6
train_data_note: SCAN instruction following and SIGMORPHON 2018 morphology (Spanish, Swahili, Turkish); few-shot setting with 4/8/16 hint examples (past/future tense); R&R learns new constructions from as few as eight initial examples
augmentation_type: R&R: recombination of original training examples via a prototype-based generative model plus resampling to encourage extrapolation; GECA used as an augmentation baseline
effect_size_notes: Paired t-tests quantify differences (see sig_test fields) but no standardized effect size is reported
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence or compositionality proxy is measured
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly addresses compositional generalization failure: vanilla seq2seq models fail on rare/unseen subsequences (e.g., past-tense tags), and R&R's learned recombination and resampling closes part of the OOD gap, enabling few-shot (8-example) learning of new compositions on SCAN and SIGMORPHON.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; the work targets compositional generalization in NLP via data augmentation.
other_metrics_reported: F1 (micro) accuracy for morphology tasks (Tables 6, 8); qualitative SCAN prediction examples (Table 12)
notes: ICLR 2021 conference paper (arXiv 2010.03706v6). SCAN results are in the body of the paper, not the excerpt, so no SCAN numbers extracted. Main-form ood value = Spanish FUT+PST (rare-tag OOD split) with recomb-2+resampling at HINTS=8, exact match 20.3% +/- 3.5%. Paired t-tests reported without Bonferroni correction (p-values down to ~1e-58). 'Several runs' averaged; seed count not stated.

title: Can Transformers Jump Around Right in Natural Language? Assessing Performance Transfer from SCAN
authors: Rahma Chaabouni; Roberto Dessì; Eugene Kharitonov
arch_detail: Vanilla Transformer with focused modifications: SAG (relative-position attention graph), convolution self-attention, fixed span, T5-style local attention with learned relative-position bias; fairseq setup with encoder/decoder normalize-before; ConvS2S-inspired localization
train_data_note: SCAN splits (jump etc.); low-resource FLoRes MT (ne-en, si-en, en-ne, en-si); newly introduced distribution-shifted compositional English-French translation task; noun-adjective order agreement dataset
effect_size_notes: No formal effect sizes; relative gains reported (13.1% BLEU low-resource, 14% COMP, 1.44% noun-adjective)
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy measured
repr_analysis_finding: Softmaxed learned relative-position biases (bij) show many heads strongly prefer fixed local positions; several heads dominantly attend to particular positions; local attention linked to SCAN compositional generalization; some heads retain ability to look beyond span, explaining T5's edge over fixed-span
repr_analysis_layer: all encoder/decoder layers, e.g. encoder layer 0 head 7, layer 2 heads 3,7; decoder layer 2 heads 3,4,5
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly investigates compositional generalization on SCAN, shows Transformer variants with localized attention (SAG+T5) jump from near-zero to ~60% SCAN-jump accuracy, and tests whether this capability transfers to low-resource and distribution-shifted MT — a direct empirical probe of when comp-gen competence matters.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; a transfer/architecture analysis across SCAN and machine translation.
other_metrics_reported: BLEU on FLoRes dev-test (ne-en 8.40+/-0.02 vs Transformer 7.94+/-0.05 for SAG+T5; en-ne 5.01+/-0.10 vs 4.43+/-0.01) and on compositional En-Fr (41.43+/-0.29 vs 40.86+/-0.34); sig at p<1e-3 and p<0.05 respectively; noun-adjective SAG +1.44% relative
notes: Bold improvements marked statistically significant over Transformer (p<1e-3 on FLoRes, p<0.05 on En-Fr) but test type unspecified; +- = 1 SEM; main-form OOD = SAG+T5 COMP 0.73+/-0.01 on compositional En-Fr; SCAN-jump best model accuracy ~60% (the instance used for attention analysis); BLEU scores kept in other_metrics_reported as they are not 0-1 proportions.

title: Learning to Generalize Compositionally by Transferring Across Semantic Parsing Tasks
authors: Wang Zhu; Peter Shaw; Tal Linzen; Fei Sha
arch_detail: DUEL algorithm: encoder and task-specific decoder layers trained on different compositional splits during pre-finetuning, then fine-tuned on the target task; encoder-decoder models T5-Base and BERT2SEQ (BERT encoder + seq2seq decoder)
train_data_note: Pre-finetuning on compositional splits (CG General, length variants) of COGS/GeoQuery/SCAN used alternately, then fine-tuning on held-out target splits; COGS_VAR variants with disjoint lexicons (1/5/10 variants) for the structural-COGS study
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; comparisons reported as exact-match percentages (e.g., 57.8% GEO TMCD with SCAN cd pre-finetuning vs 56.6% NQG-T5)
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence proxy measured; the encoder is argued to acquire a transferable inductive bias, but no probing or coherence metric is reported
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly addresses compositional generalization failure by transferring a compositional inductive bias across semantic parsing tasks (COGS, GeoQuery, SCAN); DUEL with compositional-split pre-finetuning surpasses the prior hybrid SotA on GeoQuery TMCD with a purely neural model, with ablations characterizing each step.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; framed purely as improving compositional generalization via transfer learning in semantic parsing.
limitations_extractor: No limitations section present in excerpt; COGS structural generalization noted as 'too difficult for purely neural models, even with DUEL'
open_questions_text: Future research: investigate why same-type compositional pre-finetuning splits yield only minor improvements on COGS structural generalization (4.5% to 5.2%) and develop approaches for extracting a stronger inductive bias.
other_metrics_reported: Pre-finetuning task accuracy 79.3% on structural generalization portions of COGS_VAR variants; ablation of MERGED vs DUEL pre-finetuning regimes
notes: Main-form values = headline result: GEO TMCD target split, T5-Base with SCAN cd pre-finetuning + DUEL, 57.8% (vs 56.6% NQG-T5 SotA). Table 3 (GEO len) cells partially scrambled; only prose-consistent values recorded: NONE baselines 38.6% (T5-Base) and 16.1% (BERT2SEQ), and DUEL-with-SCAN-len values 45.0% (T5-Base, +5.9 over MERGED 39.1%) and 17.7% (BERT2SEQ, +0.9 over 16.8%). COGS cg numbers recorded for structural challenge only.

title: Compositional generalization in semantic parsing with pretrained transformers
authors: A. Emin Orhan
arch_detail: T5-base and T5-3b fine-tuned on SCAN/COGS; pretraining domains varied: C4 (English), non-English corpora (marian), CodeT5 (programming languages), protein sequence modeling (pt5 base/xl)
train_data_note: SCAN and COGS, relatively small English datasets; models trained to convergence; average generalization accuracy over splits reported
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes; gains quoted as absolute percentage-point improvements (e.g., ~23% and ~73% absolute in SCAN from C4 pretraining)
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence or compositionality proxy; analysis is behavioral (downstream generalization accuracy)
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly quantifies compositional generalization failure on SCAN and COGS as a function of pretraining domain and model scale, showing pretraining (especially for larger models) narrows the OOD gap, but the study is behavioral with no mechanism, training-dynamics, or representation-level analysis of the sigma-trap.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; the work is about pretraining transfer for semantic parsing.
open_questions_text: Whether the content-specificity conditions for successful transfer can be delineated; whether pretraining generalization benefits are explainable by content-independent modifications (embedding scale, relative position sensitivity); whether transfer tasks should be more challenging (zero-shot/few-shot) to reveal pretrained knowledge.
other_metrics_reported: Relative absolute improvements: non-English pretraining ~21% absolute in COGS; protein pt5 base ~11% lower (SCAN) and ~16% lower (COGS) than t5 base scr
notes: All SCAN/COGS generalization accuracies in text are approximate (~%). Main form = T5-base with C4 pretraining on SCAN (~65%); from-scratch ~43%. No seed counts or per-split numeric tables in excerpt.

title: CNNs found to jump around more skillfully than RNNs: Compositional generalization in seq2seq convolutional networks
authors: Roberto Dessì; Marco Baroni
arch_detail: Out-of-the-box fairseq convolutional seq2seq: multi-layer CNN encoder-decoder with multi-layer attention; hyperparameter search over learning rate, layer dimensionality (128-512), layer count (6-10), kernel width (3-5), dropout (0-0.5)
train_data_note: SCAN splits: random (80/20), jump, around-right, length, turn-left; CNN tested on random, jump and around-right (length near 0%, turn-left near-perfect)
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes reported; comparisons are descriptive mean accuracies across seeds
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy measured; error analyses are behavioral, not representational
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly measures compositional generalization failure (the sigma-trap) on SCAN's jump and around-right splits, showing a CNN far outperforms RNNs, and analyzes kernel width, multi-layer attention, and error structure to explain why the CNN still does not induce systematic compositional rules.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; the paper is an architecture comparison on a compositional generalization benchmark.
limitations_text: CNN's learned positional embeddings do not generalize beyond training lengths (length split near 0%); shallow CNNs cannot handle even the random split; self-attentive networks left untested as more cumbersome to train; CNN induces no rule-like systematicity; best LSTM has 1/4 the parameters of the best CNN.
open_questions_text: Future work: investigate which CNN aspects (kernel width, multi-layer attention) are crucial for compositional generalization; formulate a tighter CNN vs LSTM comparison under matched depth and parameter budgets.
other_metrics_reported: error proportions across command words; output-length error variance under kernel-width variation; attention-layer ablation accuracies
notes: Main-form values = best-overall CNN config (LR 0.01, 6 layers, 512 dim, width-5 kernels, 0.25 dropout, 25-token batch): random 99.92%, jump 60.67%, around-right 53.25%, 5 seeds. Random split treated as ID (no systematic train/test difference). Table 2 per-split best CNN: random 100.0 +/-0.0, jump 69.2 +/-8.2, around-right 56.7 +/-10.2.

title: SUBS: Subtree Substitution for Compositional Semantic Parsing
authors: Jingfeng Yang; Le Zhang; Diyi Yang
arch_detail: Seq2seq semantic parsers: LSTM and BART-large; method = subtree substitution data augmentation (exchanging subtrees whose roots share meaning functions, gold and induced tree variants); baselines: no augmentation, SCFG recombination (Jia and Liang 2016), GECA (Andreas 2019); code at github.com/GT-SALT/SUBS
train_data_note: GeoQuery: 519 training examples (50/100/200 in few-shot scaling study); SCAN: 12,180 original + 6,660 subtree-substitution augmented examples; 3,351 of the 4,476 SCAN test examples recovered by substitution (74.87%)
augmentation_type: subtree substitution data augmentation: exchange subtrees with similar semantic function roots across training examples (gold and induced parse-tree variants)
effect_size_notes: No effect sizes; improvements reported as absolute accuracy gains (21% LSTM, 3% BART on GeoQuery Query split) and as full accuracies (e.g., 0.88 BART+SUBS)
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence metric; analysis focuses on augmented-data complexity rather than internal representations
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly attacks compositional generalization failure (the sigma-trap signature) via compositional data augmentation on SCAN and GeoQuery, raising LSTM exact match from 0% to 100% on SCAN RIGHT and reaching new SOTA on GeoQuery compositional split; limited to data-side remedies.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; the paper is a data augmentation method for semantic parsing benchmarks.
other_metrics_reported: Augmented-data complexity statistics (avg/max exchanged segment, utterance, program lengths); training-data-size scaling (Table 4); convergence speed (updates to converge)
notes: Main-form = BART-large + SUBS on GeoQuery compositional Query split (0.88, from full-519-example column of Table 4). Note: 74.87% of SCAN test examples are recoverable from augmented training data, which the paper reports transparently but does not treat as a leakage concern.

title: On graph-based reentrancy-free semantic parsing
authors: Alban Petit; Caio Corro
arch_detail: Graph-based span parser: CYK/ILP MAP inference with grammar constraints, constraint smoothing + conditional gradient solver; ~5 sentences/sec on GeoQuery; baselines: seq2seq, BERT2SEQ, BART, span-based SP
train_data_note: SCAN, GeoQuery, CLEVR standard splits: IID plus compositional splits (RIGHT, ARIGHT, TEMPLATE, LENGTH, CLOSURE); weakly-supervised latent tag anchoring discussed; dataset sizes not in excerpt
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets the sigma-trap: argues seq2seq models fail on compositional generalization splits and proposes a graph-based parser with grammar-constrained decoding that reaches 100% on SCAN generalization and outperforms span-based parsing on GeoQuery/CLEVR, though the length split remains hard; no link to training dynamics or flatness.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; a semantic parsing methodology paper with complexity proofs and benchmark evaluations.
limitations_text: Parser speed is a downside (~5 sentences per second on GeoQuery); accuracy is still significantly worse on the split requiring generalization to longer programs.
open_questions_text: Extensions for ASTs containing reentrancies; cases where a single word anchors more than one predicate or entity; more general research on neural architectures that generalize better to longer sentences.
other_metrics_reported: Exact match accuracy (with and without CPLEX rounding heuristic); denotation accuracy with corrected GeoQuery executor; NP-hardness proofs for MAP inference and latent tag anchoring
notes: Table 1 flattening loses row breaks in the our-approach block; only confidently aligned cells reported. Ours: SCAN denotation 100 (ARIGHT), GeoQuery IID 100, GeoQuery LENGTH 74.9 (vs span-based 63.6; could be corrected-executor value). Baselines rows clean. CLEVR (IID/CLOSURE) evaluated but not in task vocabulary; excluded from sub_experiments.

title: LAGr: Labeling Aligned Graphs for Improving Systematic Generalization in Semantic Parsing
authors: Dora Jambor; Dzmitry Bahdanau
arch_detail: LAGr graph-labeling parser: predicts node and edge labels for a multi-layer input-aligned graph using a shared Transformer encoder; PED (positional embedding downscaling) init; weakly-supervised variant with approximate MAP alignment via Hungarian matching (K candidates, noise sigma)
train_data_note: CFQ MCD1/MCD2/MCD3 splits + random split (used as in-distribution for tuning); COGS train/gen sets. Metric is graph accuracy (predicted vs true graph isomorphism), comparable to exact-match accuracy of prior work
schema_coherence_notes: No representation-level coherence/compositionality proxy; LAGr changes output structure (graph labeling), not internal representations
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure (the sigma-trap) on COGS and CFQ: LAGr graph-labeling raises CFQ MCD mean from ~18% seq2seq baselines to ~39% and beats all baselines on every MCD split, but does not study training dynamics, flatness, or representation-level schema coherence.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI alignment, safety, or goal misgeneralization; a semantic-parsing method paper concerned only with compositional accuracy.
limitations_text: Weakly-supervised LAGr does not always converge on the training set; runs not reaching 99.5% training graph accuracy (~12%) were discarded. Duplicate node labels in 3.7-5.7% of CFQ examples complicate alignment inference (fixes 2.7% hard article cases via cached alignment candidate). Lexicons not integrated.
open_questions_text: Future work: modify LAGr to condition edge predictions on node labels (based on error analysis); use a pretrained encoder; apply more advanced discrete optimization or amortized inference methods for alignment; lexicons can be integrated though not expected to help on COGS.
notes: Main-form values = best weakly-supervised LAGr config (K=5, sigma=10) on CFQ: ID=random split 99.7 (sd 0.0), OOD=mean over MCD1 62.8, MCD2 30.3, MCD3 25.4. Excerpt results table garbled; layout confirmed against arXiv source, all numbers present in excerpt. 8-11 runs per split reported; n_seeds recorded as 10. Optimizer not specified in excerpt. COGS results only qualitative in excerpt.

title: ReaSCAN: Compositional Reasoning in Language Grounding
authors: Zhengxuan Wu; Elisa Kreiss; Desmond C. Ong; Christopher Potts

title: A Benchmark for Systematic Generalization in Grounded Language Understanding
authors: Laura Ruis; Jacob Andreas; Marco Baroni; Diane Bouchacourt; Brenden M. Lake

title: Compositional generalization through meta sequence-to-sequence learning
authors: Brenden M. Lake
arch_detail: Memory-augmented seq2seq (LSTM encoder-decoder + external memory + decoder attention; 'seq2seq recurrent' per excerpt); baselines: standard seq2seq RNN, syntactic-attention Transformer
train_data_note: SCAN; meta-training on episodes of 4 primitives sampled from 24 (plus direction variants in Exp 4.5); seq2seq training augmented with 20 extra primitive/action pairs; length split trains on ~17,000 instructions (<=22 actions)

title: Can Large Reasoning Models do Analogical Reasoning under Perceptual Uncertainty?

title: Compositional Generalization via Semantic Tagging

relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets compositional generalization failure (sigma-trap): standard seq2seq semantic parsers fail on unseen compositions of seen components, and the semantic-tagging two-stage decoding framework improves compositional generalization across architectures (Transformer, LSTM, RoBERTa) and semantic formalisms, though it still fails on unseen syntactic structure.

relevance_sigma_justification: Provides a formal kernel theory of when compositional structure fails to yield compositional generalization (the sigma-trap): it proves compositionally structured kernel models are restricted to conjunction-wise additive functions, identifies two concrete failure modes (memorization leak and shortcut bias) driven by training-data statistics, and shows when very deep networks memorize rather than generalize; relevance tempered by the absence of benchmark-scale empirical results in the excerpt.

title: Learning to Compose Representations of Different Encoder Layers towards Improving Compositional Generalization
authors: Lei Lin; Shuangtao Li; Yafang Zheng; Biao Fu; Shan Liu; Yidong Chen; Xiaodong Shi
task_custom_name: CoGnition (Chinese-English MT, CG-test set; not in task vocabulary)

title: Systematic Generalization on gSCAN with Language Conditioned Embedding
authors: Tong Gao; Qi Huang; Raymond J. Mooney

title: On a Built-in Conflict between Deep Learning and Systematic Generalization
authors: Yuanpeng Li

title: Learning Algebraic Representation for Systematic Generalization in Abstract Reasoning

title: From Reasoning Traces to Reusable Modules: Understanding Compositional Generalization in Language Model Reasoning

title: Compositional generalization by factorizing alignment and translation
authors: Russin, J.; Jo, J.; O’Reilly, R.C.; Bengio, Y.
venue: Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
arch_detail: Syntactic Attention: seq2seq GRU with separate alignment and translation modules via dependency attention (modification of GRU+attention); baselines GRU+attn, GRU+attn-dep, LSTM
train_data_note: SCAN add-jump split with 1/2/4/8/16/32 'jump' commands in training and template splits (jump around right, primitive right/opposite right/around right)
repr_analysis_finding: Attention visualizations on the add-jump split show the Syntactic Attention model applies training-sentence alignment patterns to test sentences containing the novel verb 'jump'; the depicted failure case (Fig 14) attends to the wrong command sequence.
relevance_sigma_justification: Directly targets the sigma-trap: SCAN compositional generalization failures of standard RNNs are addressed by an alignment/translation factorization inductive bias, with quantitative results across add-jump and template splits showing the model substantially outperforms standard recurrent baselines on several splits.
relevance_alignment_justification: No connection to AI safety, alignment, or goal misgeneralization; the work targets compositional generalization for its own sake.
notes: ACL 2020 Student Research Workshop. No ID accuracy reported; all values are OOD test accuracies. Add-jump sub_experiments report the 1-jump-command condition; full sweep in notes. Means over 5 random jump-command samples (hint said 25). Template tables reproduce Loula et al. baselines.

title: Neural Collapse Inspired Feature Alignment for Out-of-Distribution Generalization
authors: Chen, Z.; Zhang, M.; Cui, S.; Li, H.; Niu, G.; Gong, M.; Zhang, C.; Zhang, K.
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
task_custom_name: Spurious-correlation OOD classification (ColoredMNIST, ColoredCOCO, COCOPlaces, NICO)
arch_detail: Backbone architectures not specified in excerpt; method learns per-environment local models and applies semantic masks to inputs at pixel or feature level
train_data_note: Three toy datasets (ColoredMNIST, ColoredCOCO, COCOPlaces) and one real dataset (NICO); samples partitioned into environments either by known labels or by learned local models with maximum-likelihood assignment
schema_coherence_notes: Method enforces neural collapse to a simplex equiangular tight frame (ETF) on semantic-mask features as a training objective, but the excerpt reports no empirical measurement of a representation-level coherence proxy
relevance_sigma_justification: Addresses OOD generalization failure under spurious correlation via environment partitioning and neural-collapse-based feature alignment, improving OOD accuracy on four benchmarks; relevant to distribution-shift robustness but not to compositional generalization or schema coherence, and it does not analyze training-dynamics geometry beyond imposing the ETF constraint.
relevance_alignment_justification: OOD robustness is an indirect safety-relevant capability, but the paper does not address goal misgeneralization, alignment, or value learning; its connection to AI alignment is only via improved distribution-shift robustness.
open_questions_text: Investigate more effective and efficient environment partitioning techniques; apply the method to other domains such as segmentation and few-shot spurious correlation issues.
notes: Reports only OOD accuracy (mean +/- SD) on ColoredMNIST, ColoredCOCO, COCOPlaces, NICO for Ours and Ours (w/o env) against 16 baselines (ERM, IRM, VREx, GroupDRO, etc.); no ID accuracy, no seed counts, no significance tests.
